title: Unsupervised clustering splits Ethiopian rainfall into ten seasonal regimes
summary: Ward hierarchical and K-means clustering of 1981-2022 monthly rainfall, temperature and elevation from the Ethiopian Meteorological Institute's 4 km merged gridded data (more than 66,000 points) grouped Ethiopia into ten rainy-season regimes, with the number of clusters chosen by the elbow method, and the regimes were converted into a dry, short-rainy and main-rainy seasonal timetable. Agreement between the two clustering methods was checked monthly with the Adjusted Rand Index. Earlier station-based studies proposed five to eight zones; this preprint reports no validation against independent station records or forecasts, so the regimes are descriptive and not yet shown to improve forecasting or planning.
ai_technology: Unsupervised clustering (Ward hierarchical and K-means) of gridded climate variables with elbow-method cluster selection.
organization: Addis Ababa University; Ethiopian Meteorological Institute; Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT

evidence.tested: Retrospective clustering of 1981-2022 gridded data with Adjusted Rand Index agreement between two clustering methods.
evidence.unknown: No independent validation against station observations or forecasts; cluster number choice partly subjective; not peer reviewed; descriptive regionalization.
evidence.ai_role: Unsupervised clustering produces the regime map and seasonal timetable from the climate fields.
